A desert country between the Caspian Sea and the Amu Darya, independent since October 1991. The map shows it in 1994 and 2010.

The Turkmen descend from the Oghuz tribes, and their land holds the ruins of Merv, once one of the great cities of the Islamic world. Russia conquered it in the 1880s, and in Soviet times it was the Turkmen republic.

At independence the Communist party chief Saparmurat Niyazov took the title Turkmenbashi, leader of the Turkmen, and built one of the world's strongest personality cults. He renamed months after himself and his mother, and made his book, the Ruhnama, required reading in schools. In 1995 the United Nations recognised the country's permanent neutrality.

After Niyazov died in 2006, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow took over, and in 2022 his son succeeded him. The state lives mainly on natural gas, among the largest reserves in the world, sold since 2009 through the pipeline to China. The capital, Ashgabat, has been rebuilt in white marble.
